authority.issuer_authenticity: signed ingress claims verified at bind by the configured Ed25519 host policy
authority.receipt_authenticity: host-owned durable ledger; receipt_id is a content digest, not a digital signature

scope.run_response: execution_receipt is returned only after its ledger write succeeds
scope.receipt_lookup: op=receipt retrieves a validated record by receipt_id from the host ledger; optional shape and values compare with the recorded output
scope.exact_output_transport: durable run also returns output_f32_le_base64; receipt lookup accepts that encoding with shape to preserve f32 bits across JSON
scope.checkpoint_export: op=checkpoint exports exact stateful multi-input ProgramBundle bytes as base64 only when enabled by a trusted runner startup option and current signed inputs
scope.unsigned_and_process_only_modes: run and verify behavior unchanged; no durable host execution receipt
scope.verify_operation: existing numerical verification remains separate; it does not issue an execution receipt

proof_state.identity: SHA-256 over canonical ordered JSON receipt fields excluding receipt_id
fields: restore_event_id (optional when a restore is active)
proof_state.input_claims: sorted slot, source, role, shape, f32 value digest, revision and SHA-256 of each verified canonical signed claim; state inputs may also identify a durable host handoff record
proof_state.output: exact f32 little-endian SHA-256 and four-dimensional output shape observed from WASM
proof_state.program_identity: exact graph.programIdentity JSON, which excludes mutable layer state
proof_state.state_checkpoint_bytes_sha256: SHA-256 of the exact exported multi-input ProgramBundle bytes, including plan, structural identity, layer initialization records, and mutable layer state
proof_state.state_parent_receipt_id: when present, the immediately preceding committed internal runtime state; it is the restored receipt for the first run after restore
proof_state.restore_event_id: when present, the committed host restore event identifying the selected checkpoint and its execution-order anchor; see host-checkpoint-restore.v1.json
proof_state.checkpoint_digest_scope: byte-level correlation only; not semantic state identity, state authentication, or authorization
proof_state.history_validation: ledger reopening validates receipt ID, schema, checkpoint digest format, monotonic sequence and the referenced claims as latest at the recorded claim_count

valid_transitions: all required signed input claims are current while the exclusive ledger lock is held
Burn executes the graph and the host observes output shape and f32 values
the host exports a stateful multi-input ProgramBundle and hashes its exact bytes
the host atomically commits the v2 receipt to the same private ledger before replying
a failed receipt commit returns an error; no success response or durable receipt is asserted
later input revisions cannot rewrite an earlier valid historical receipt
successful subsequent runs in one session advance the immediate state parent to the previous successful receipt
limits: A failed receipt commit can occur after numerical execution; the runner does not claim numerical rollback or exactly-once side effects.
JSON numeric values cannot distinguish negative zero from positive zero; use output_f32_le_base64 for exact output comparison.
A content hash detects changed bytes but a privileged writer of the host ledger can rewrite its history.
The bundle has no signature or authentication; valid mutable-state byte changes can be accepted by import.
A checkpoint digest does not say that two different Burn state byte streams have different semantic meaning, and does not identify equivalent states.
Program identity remains structural and excludes mutable layer state; the separate checkpoint digest binds the serialized state bytes observed for this run.
A receipt can supply exact output bytes to the Node durable state-handoff path; the handoff record does not authorize actions or state promotion.
A 50,000-receipt or 32 MiB ledger limit fails closed for new durable run receipts.
